identity.description: Fully-connected feed-forward neural network trained by backprop (Adam/SGD/L-BFGS). A universal approximator whose capacity is set by hidden_layer_sizes; on typical business-tabular data it needs careful scaling, enough rows to feed its weight count, and usually fights gradient-boosting for the same slot rather than beating it.

emits.note: softmax outputs — smooth but typically OVERCONFIDENT when the net has capacity to overfit; better-shaped than NB's but still worth external calibration for threshold work

alpha.note: L2 penalty — the primary capacity brake

solver.note: lbfgs converges better on small n; adam scales

max_iter.note: raised from sklearn's 200 default — the stock value routinely ends in ConvergenceWarning

early_stopping.note: holds out 10% for validation-loss stopping — the cheap overfit brake

invariances.why: gradient descent multiplies each weight's gradient by its input's magnitude — unscaled features give an ill-conditioned loss surface, and the default weight initialization assumes roughly unit-scale inputs; without standardization training is slow, unstable, or fails outright
the first layer computes affine combinations of raw values — a log or rank transform changes every pre-activation and hence the fit
a NaN input propagates through every affine layer and poisons the loss; sklearn raises on NaN
the input layer is a real-valued vector — categoricals must be encoded (no embedding layer in the sklearn implementation)
a universal approximator trained on empirical risk — no likelihood assumed on the inputs or errors

even the default (100,) architecture carries thousands of weights; on small n it memorizes, and on small-to-mid tabular data it is repeatedly outperformed by gradient boosting — it earns its keep from tens of thousands of rows up

a ReLU network is globally piecewise-affine — outside the training hull the active linear piece extends indefinitely, so it extrapolates linearly and with unwarranted confidence, giving no signal that it left the data

featureStats.why: n divided by the weight count implied by hidden_layer_sizes is the memorization ratio — below a few rows per weight the net can fit noise exactly, the direct capacity gate
gradient conditioning degrades with the spread of input scales — a large ratio predicts the slow/failed convergence that standardization prevents
cross-entropy on a skewed problem is minimized by drifting toward the majority prior; flags class weighting/resampling and PR-based metrics

modelMetrics.why: a widening train-vs-validation loss gap is the direct overfit signature of a high-capacity net — the signal to raise alpha or shrink the architecture
a loss_curve_ still descending at max_iter means training was truncated, not converged — the reported score understates the model and the iteration budget is the fix
the loss surface is non-convex and the fit starts from random weights — high variance across seeds means the single reported score is an unreliable draw, an ensembling/restart signal

edgeCases.behavior: ill-conditioned gradients — ConvergenceWarning, plateaued loss, or divergence
weight count exceeds information in the data — memorizes, unstable CV
silently returns the truncated fit with a warning
edgeCases.note: raise max_iter or enable early_stopping; treat the warning as a red flag, not noise

edgeCases.behavior: dead ReLUs — units stuck at zero output, capacity silently lost
edgeCases.note: lower learning_rate_init or switch to tanh

edgeCases.behavior: different seeds land in different local minima — run-to-run score spread
edgeCases.note: fix random_state for reproducibility; average restarts for robustness

driver.threadSafety: fit uses BLAS threading internally; predict is thread-safe

canBeSeeds.note: repairs the softmax overconfidence of an overfit net
a genuinely good bagging citizen — the non-convex, seed-sensitive fit is exactly the instability bagging averages away

placementClaims.why: no native NaN handling — a missing value poisons every downstream activation
symmetrizing heavy-tailed features keeps extreme values from saturating activations and dominating early gradients
scale-sensitive by mechanism — gradient conditioning and the unit-scale weight-init assumption make standardization a precondition for reliable convergence
the input layer takes real vectors; categoricals must be one-hot/ordinal encoded (no embeddings in sklearn's MLP)
